title: Motivating Question (Introduction)
statement_text: Let $m\ge2$ and let $H$ be a fixed graph with $\chi(H)=k>m$. For which values of $p$ is it true that $\mathrm{ex}(G(n,p), K_m, H) = (1+o(1))\binom{k-1}{m}\left(\frac{n}{k-1}\right)^m p^{\binom{m}{2}}$ w.h.p.?
context_text: For graphs $T$ and $H$, $\mathrm{ex}(n,T,H)$ is the maximum number of copies of $T$ in an $H$-free subgraph of $K_n$, and $\mathrm{ex}(G(n,p),T,H)$ is the random variable equal to the maximum number of copies of $T$ in an $H$-free subgraph of the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$; w.h.p. means with probability tending to 1 as $n\to\infty$, and $f\gg g$ means $f/g\to\infty$. The 2-density of $H$ is $m_2(H)=\max\{\frac{e(H')-1}{v(H')-2}: H'\subseteq H, v(H')\ge3\}$; note $m_2(K_m)=\frac{m+1}{2}$. Alon and Shikhelman showed $\mathrm{ex}(n,K_m,H)=(1+o(1))\binom{k-1}{m}(\frac{n}{k-1})^m$ when $\chi(H)=k>m$ (attained by the balanced $(k-1)$-partite graph), so the question asks when the random analogue matches the deterministic count times $p^{\binom m2}$. For $T=K_2$ the answer (Conlon–Gowers, Schacht) is that $\mathrm{ex}(G(n,p),H)=(1-\frac{1}{\chi(H)-1}+o(1))\binom n2p$ for $p\gg n^{-1/m_2(H)}$, while for $p\ll n^{-1/m_2(H)}$ almost all edges can be kept. The authors prove that if $m_2(H)\ge m_2(K_m)$ the formula holds w.h.p. for $p\gg n^{-1/m_2(H)}$, and if $m_2(H)>m_2(K_m)$ then $\mathrm{ex}(G(n,p),K_m,H)=(1+o(1))\binom nm p^{\binom m2}$ for $p\ll n^{-1/m_2(H)}$; this covers every $H$ with $\chi(H)\ge m+2$. When $\chi(H)=m+1$ there are infinitely many $H$ with $m_2(H)<m_2(K_m)$, and for some of them almost all copies of $K_m$ can still be kept for $p\le n^{-1/m_2(H)+\delta}$, so the critical value of $p$ is bounded away from $n^{-1/m_2(H)}$ and its exact location is left open. In their concluding remarks the authors suggest that the transition should occur when $n^{m-2}p^{\binom m2}$ crosses $n^{-1/m_2(H)}$, based on the random graph formed by the edges lying in copies of $K_m$.
